intent.raw_query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June from Chicago

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, fresh pasta, and local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and street food stalls. This bohemian neighborhood offers the most authentic Roman culinary experience away from tourist traps.

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Tour
experiences.description: Visit this intimate yet world-class gallery housing Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings inside a baroque villa. Reservations are mandatory and entry is limited to 360 visitors at a time, ensuring an unhurried, immersive experience with masterpieces like Apollo and Daphne.

experiences.name: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. Sample porchetta sandwiches, aged pecorino romano, cured meats, and the famously divisive quinto quarto (offal dishes) that define true Roman cucina povera tradition.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk
experiences.description: Stroll through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire across the Forum and Palatine Hill, where emperors once lived. Combined with Colosseum entry, this archaeological complex offers unparalleled insight into Roman history and culture, with panoramic views over ruins that inspired Renaissance artists for centuries.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 16:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome (Georgia) Airport at 16:00 on Condor flight. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport, and check in to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome at 15 Chateau Drive. Freshen up and get settled in your room.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll around the local area near the hotel to get your bearings. Explore the nearby streets of Rome, GA, and window-shop along Broad Street in downtown Rome, which is about 5-10 minutes from the hotel area.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Meal on the plane or airport food before/during travel
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli or Harvest Moon Cafe near downtown Rome, GA - budget-friendly local spots offering hearty meals under $15 per person. Alternatively, grab a quick and affordable bite at a nearby Zaxby's or Chick-fil-A for under $10.

day_by_day.notes: Since this is arrival day, keep things light. Confirm your hotel check-in, pick up a local map or use Google Maps to plan the week ahead. The weather in June averages 29.8°C so stay hydrated. Pack light clothing for the heat. Note: This itinerary is based in Rome, Georgia, USA (per the hotel coordinates 34.2212, -85.1513), not Rome, Italy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chieftains Museum & Major Ridge Home (501 Riverside Pkwy NE) - a fascinating historic site and National Historic Landmark that is free or very low cost. Explore the Cherokee heritage and early American history exhibits. Open from 10:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Rome Area History Museum (305 Broad St) in downtown Rome for a deep dive into local art and history. Admission is budget-friendly (typically under $5). Afterwards, walk along the scenic Oostanaula Riverfront Park and enjoy the outdoor public art installations along the riverwalk - completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Rome's Broad Street for evening entertainment. Visit local galleries or pop into any open studios. Enjoy the cooler evening air along the river.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at La Quinta by Wyndham (included with most La Quinta stays - take full advantage to save money)
meals.lunch: Harvest Moon Cafe on Broad Street - known for fresh, local ingredients and affordable lunch specials around $10-$13
meals.dinner: Amici Italian Restaurant in downtown Rome - authentic Italian-inspired dishes that tie into your art and food interests, with pasta dishes starting around $12-$16

day_by_day.notes: June heat will be intense (near 30°C). Start morning activities early around 9-10 AM before peak heat. Carry a refillable water bottle. Downtown Rome is very walkable so you can save on transport costs today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Shorter University Art Gallery (315 Shorter Ave) - free admission to view rotating art exhibitions featuring regional and student artwork. A wonderful budget-friendly art experience. Explore the beautiful Shorter Hill campus grounds afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or rideshare to Berry College (2277 Martha Berry Hwy) - one of the world's largest college campuses with stunning Gothic architecture, a working farm, and beautiful grounds open to the public for free. Explore the Ford Buildings, the historic mill, and the scenic Viking Mountain area. Great for photography and art inspiration.
day_by_day.evening: Return to downtown Rome for the Friday evening scene. Check if there are any local art walks, live music events, or farmers market events happening on Broad Street (Rome often hosts weekend events in summer).

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at La Quinta by Wyndham
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch from a local grocery store (Kroger or Publix nearby) - grab sandwiches, fruit, and drinks for under $8 total and enjoy on Berry College's beautiful grounds
meals.dinner: El Molino Mexican Restaurant in Rome - generous portions of authentic Mexican food, very budget-friendly with entrees around $10-$13. Excellent value for money.

day_by_day.notes: Berry College is a must-see for art and architecture lovers - it's completely free to visit and the grounds are spectacular. Bring sunscreen and a hat for the afternoon outdoor exploration. Check Berry College's website for any summer events or exhibitions.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Rome Farmers Market (if running on Saturdays - typically at the Civic Center area) for local produce, handmade crafts, and artisan food products. A great way to experience local food culture on a budget. Browse and sample local goods for free or spend a few dollars on fresh snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Clock Tower and the Three Rivers area - Rome's iconic landmark at the top of Myrtle Hill is free to visit and offers panoramic views of the three rivers (Etowah, Oostanaula, and Coosa). Also visit the Confederate Cemetery and Myrtle Hill Cemetery which have interesting historic art and sculpture. Walk the Riverwalk trail along the Coosa River for free outdoor recreation.
day_by_day.evening: Attend any local Saturday evening events in downtown Rome. Check the Rome-Floyd Parks & Recreation or Downtown Rome events calendar for free or low-cost concerts, outdoor movies, or art events that often take place on summer Saturday evenings.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at La Quinta by Wyndham
meals.lunch: Sample food from the Farmers Market for a fun, budget-friendly lunch experience ($8-$12 for a full spread of local goodies)
meals.dinner: Schroeder's New Deli (101 E 2nd Ave) - a Rome institution with generous sandwiches, soups, and deli plates. Very affordable with most items under $12. Perfect budget dinner with great local character.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a great day to soak in local culture. The Three Rivers area and Clock Tower are completely free and offer beautiful views - perfect for photography. The evening in downtown Rome on weekends tends to be lively, especially in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Coosa Valley Art Museum or explore the public murals and street art throughout downtown Rome - Rome has invested in public art installations that are completely free to enjoy. Download a self-guided walking tour map from the Rome Tourism website and spend the morning discovering outdoor art around the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive approximately 45 minutes to Calhoun, GA to visit the New Echota State Historic Site (1211 Chatsworth Hwy NE) - a significant Cherokee cultural and art history site with very low admission (typically $5 or less). Alternatively, visit the Etowah Indian Mounds State Historic Site in Cartersville (about 45 min away) for ancient Native American art and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome and enjoy a quiet Sunday evening. Browse local bookshops or gift shops in downtown Rome for locally made art prints and souvenirs within budget.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at La Quinta by Wyndham
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the hotel area grocery store before the day trip to save money ($6-$8 for sandwiches and snacks)
meals.dinner: Tremont House Restaurant or a local pizza spot in Rome for a relaxed Sunday dinner. Look for Sunday specials - many Rome restaurants offer discounted Sunday menus. Budget around $12-$15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If visiting Etowah Indian Mounds, wear comfortable walking shoes as there is significant outdoor terrain. The mounds themselves are impressive ancient art and architecture. Bring plenty of water for the June heat. Check opening hours before visiting as some historic sites have limited Sunday hours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Rome-Floyd County Library and its art collection - many public libraries host rotating art exhibitions for free. Afterward, walk through the Broad Street Historic District photographing the beautiful 19th-century architecture, which is an art form in itself. Pick up a self-guided historic walking tour brochure from the Rome Tourism office (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Cave Spring area (about 20 minutes from Rome) to visit the Rolater Park and the natural cave - a unique geological and natural art experience. The cave tour is very affordable (typically $3-$5). The park also has a natural spring pool for swimming to cool off from the June heat. Bring a swimsuit!
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for a final evening of downtown exploration. Visit any local art galleries that may be open for evening hours, or simply enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Broad Street.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at La Quinta by Wyndham
meals.lunch: Grab a budget-friendly lunch at one of the Cave Spring local eateries or pack a picnic for Rolater Park ($6-$10)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at The Forrest Restaurant or another well-reviewed Rome restaurant - look for weekday specials and keep the bill under $20 per person by choosing wisely from the menu

day_by_day.notes: Cave Spring and Rolater Park is a hidden gem near Rome - the natural swimming pool is a wonderful way to cool down in June heat while experiencing something unique. Bring cash as some smaller attractions in Cave Spring may not accept cards. The cave tour is a fun, affordable, and memorable experience.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning revisiting your favorite spots in downtown Rome. Pick up locally made art prints, pottery, or food souvenirs from shops along Broad Street as budget-friendly mementos. Visit the Rome Area Council for the Arts (RACA) if open - they often have exhibitions and information about local artists.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a final scenic drive or walk along the Riverwalk for last views of the three rivers confluence - one of Rome's most beautiful and free natural attractions. Reflect on the week's experiences and take final photos. Begin packing and preparing for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner in Rome before any onward travel arrangements. Check out of the hotel if departing or relax at the property.

meals.breakfast: Complimentary breakfast at La Quinta by Wyndham - make the most of it on your last morning
meals.lunch: Broad Street Baking Company or a local cafe for a light, affordable farewell lunch ($8-$12) - try a local specialty pastry or sandwich as a final taste of Rome, GA
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite restaurant from the week for a farewell meal, or try somewhere new on Broad Street. Budget $12-$18 per person for a satisfying final dinner.

day_by_day.notes: This is your last full day so make it count! Rome, Georgia is a surprisingly rich destination for art and food lovers on a budget. Total estimated daily food budget: $20-$35 per day using the complimentary hotel breakfast. Total attraction costs for the week: approximately $20-$30 for all paid admissions. The city's walkable downtown, free public art, historic sites, and natural beauty make it an excellent budget destination. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Rome Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — arrival day. Flight lands at 16:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome airport at 16:00. Collect luggage, clear customs, and transfer to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome (~30–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Take a leisurely stroll around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings and shake off travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk: Ease into Rome's culinary scene with a guided evening stroll through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, and local wines at atmospheric stops. A perfect, low-effort introduction after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — multiple tastings across the neighborhood. Budget ~€35–50 per person including the tour.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk in advance as evening slots fill quickly in June. Wear comfortable walking shoes. June evenings are warm (~22–24°C) so light clothing is fine. Keep euros handy for any extra drinks or snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Start early (book a 9:00 AM entry slot) to beat the crowds. Spend 3–4 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections — from the Gallery of Maps and Raphael Rooms to Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Arrive 15 minutes early to queue at the entrance.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber and explore the Castel Sant'Angelo and the charming Prati neighborhood. Browse the boutique shops along Via Cola di Rienzo. Rest briefly at a café before heading onward.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across the iconic Ponte Sant'Angelo at golden hour for beautiful views of the Tiber, then make your way to a traditional Roman trattoria in the Prati district for a relaxed sit-down dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — grab a cornetto and cappuccino at a local bar (~€3–5).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the Vatican — try a panino or pizza al taglio from a local bakery in Prati (~€8–12). Avoid tourist traps immediately outside the Vatican.
meals.dinner: Trattoria Pizzarium-area or Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — classic Roman dishes like cacio e pepe, saltimbocca, and tiramisu. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets MUST be pre-booked online — same-day entry is nearly impossible in June. The Sistine Chapel prohibits photography; be respectful of the rules. Wear covered shoulders and knees (required for entry). Carry water — it gets hot waiting in lines even in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour: Book a timed-entry slot (9:00 or 11:00 AM — mandatory, max 2 hours per visit). Marvel at Bernini's extraordinary sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in this intimate yet world-class villa gallery. Arrive 15 minutes early as latecomers are not admitted.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy the surrounding Villa Borghese gardens — rent a rowboat on the lake, or simply walk through the shaded parkland. Head down to the Spanish Steps and the Trevi Fountain area for classic Rome sightseeing. Toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain and explore the surrounding streets of the historic center.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Piazza Navona area as the sun sets and street artists and musicians come alive. Find a restaurant in the Campo de' Fiori neighborhood for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near the hotel — cornetto, fresh orange juice, cappuccino (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Picnic in the Villa Borghese gardens — pick up fresh bread, cheese, cured meats, and fruit from a nearby alimentari (deli) or Mercato Trionfale (~€10–15 per person). A delightful mid-range option.
meals.dinner: Ristorante or trattoria near Campo de' Fiori — try pasta alla carbonara or coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew). Budget ~€28–40 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance in June — book as soon as possible. The gallery only allows 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for the afternoon's extensive walking. Stay hydrated — afternoon temperatures can reach 29–30°C.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk: Head to the ancient heart of the Roman Empire. Walk through the Forum where Julius Caesar was cremated, climb Palatine Hill for sweeping panoramic views over Rome, and explore ruins of imperial palaces. Allocate 3–4 hours for a thorough visit. Consider an audio guide or guided tour for historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit near the Colosseum and take in its iconic exterior (book a timed entry if you wish to go inside — add ~1 hour). Explore the Circus Maximus and the Aventine Hill neighborhood. Visit the famous Knights of Malta keyhole on Aventine Hill for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome.
day_by_day.evening: Testaccio neighborhood is just below Aventine Hill — perfect for an authentic Roman evening. Explore the lively Testaccio piazzas and grab aperitivo before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel — classic Roman breakfast bar style, quick and affordable (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Grab street food near the Forum area — suppli, pizza bianca, or a tramezzino sandwich from a nearby bar (~€8–12). Alternatively, pack snacks to eat in the Forum grounds.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Testaccio — one of Rome's most authentic food neighborhoods. Try Flavio al Velavevodetto or Da Remo for classic Roman pizza and pasta. Budget ~€22–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Combo tickets for the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill are available and represent good value (~€18–22). Pre-book online to skip queues. Wear sunscreen and a hat — the Forum and Palatine Hill are largely exposed with minimal shade. Saturday evenings in Testaccio are lively and fun.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour: Dive deep into Rome's culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's most authentic covered food market. Join a guided food tour to taste Roman street food specialties — supplì, porchetta, trapizzino, aged pecorino, and the famous offal dishes that define Roman cucina povera. A fascinating and delicious morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, visit the nearby Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) — a surprisingly peaceful and beautiful spot where Keats and Shelley are buried. Then explore the Ostiense neighborhood and its vibrant street art scene along Via del Porto Fluviale. Visit the Centrale Montemartini museum — a unique former power plant housing ancient Roman sculptures.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the historic center for a sunset walk along the Lungotevere (Tiber embankment). End the evening with gelato and a stroll through Piazza del Popolo or the elegant Via Condotti area.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a quick café stop before the food tour — you'll be eating plenty during the tour!
meals.lunch: Largely covered by the Testaccio Food Tour tastings (confirm with tour operator). Top up with a light snack if needed — arancini or a slice of pizza (~€5–8).
meals.dinner: Gelateria for dessert-as-dinner evening — try Fatamorgana or Giolitti for artisan gelato (~€4–6). Follow with a casual aperitivo at a wine bar in the Pigneto or Ostiense area. Budget ~€15–25 for a relaxed Sunday evening.

day_by_day.notes: The Testaccio Market is open Tuesday–Sunday mornings; arrive by 9:00–10:00 AM for the best experience before stalls start closing. Centrale Montemartini is closed on Mondays — perfect timing for a Sunday visit. Sunday evenings in Rome are relaxed and family-oriented — a lovely contrast to the busy weekdays.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Jewish Ghetto and Largo di Torre Argentina — visit the ancient Roman temple ruins (now a cat sanctuary) and the historic synagogue area. Browse the antique bookshops and artisan workshops along Via dei Giubbonari. Visit the beautiful Sant'Andrea della Valle church with its stunning baroque interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross to the Pantheon (free entry, book a timed slot) — marvel at the 2,000-year-old unreinforced concrete dome, still the world's largest. Then explore the charming streets of the Monti neighborhood — Rome's bohemian quarter full of independent boutiques, vintage shops, and artisan studios. Browse the market stalls at Piazza della Madonna dei Monti.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour in Monti — join locals at one of the neighborhood's many wine bars for Aperol Spritz and complimentary snacks. Then enjoy a leisurely dinner at a restaurant in Monti, one of Rome's most characterful dining neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local cornetteria in the neighborhood (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Traditional Jewish-Roman cuisine in the Ghetto — try fried artichokes alla giudia, salt cod (baccalà), or ricotta-filled pastries at a local trattoria. Budget ~€18–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Monti neighborhood — try Trattoria Monti for classic Roman-Marchigiana cuisine or Alle Carrette for excellent pizza. Budget ~€25–38 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now charges a small entry fee (~€5) and requires a timed reservation — book online in advance. Monday mornings are quieter at many sites as some museums are closed, making it ideal for outdoor and neighborhood exploration. Monti is best explored on foot — the streets are narrow and pedestrian-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore anything you missed. Consider a visit to the Galleria Doria Pamphilj (a hidden gem with Velázquez and Caravaggio works, often overlooked by tourists) near the Corso. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at the artisan shops around Campo de' Fiori or the Monti market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a long, leisurely final lunch at a beloved Roman trattoria — savor the flavors one last time. After lunch, begin making your way back to the hotel to collect luggage and prepare for departure. Allow ample time for transfer to the airport depending on your flight schedule.
day_by_day.evening: Departure evening — head to the airport. If time allows before transfer, enjoy a final gelato or espresso at a classic Roman café. Buon viaggio!

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a final cornetto and cappuccino at a local bar — enjoy the ritual one last time (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Splurge slightly on a memorable farewell lunch — try Ristorante Il Sorpasso or a well-reviewed trattoria in the historic center. Order pasta, a secondo, and finish with tiramisù. Budget ~€30–45 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or light snacks if departing in the evening — budget accordingly (~€10–20).

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in from central Rome. Rome's Fiumicino (FCO) airport is ~45–60 minutes from the city center by train or taxi. Confirm your departure terminal in advance. Pack any food purchases (vacuum-sealed cured meats, hard cheeses, olive oil) carefully to comply with airline and customs regulations.

day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome (Condor flight lands 16:00). Transfer by private luxury car service to La Quinta by Wyndham Rome. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room. Take a gentle evening stroll around the immediate hotel surroundings to acclimate and enjoy the warm June air (avg. high ~30°C).
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk – Join a guided premium evening tour through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere, sampling supplì (fried rice balls), Roman artichokes, aged pecorino, and local Frascati wines. A perfect, leisurely introduction to Roman culinary culture after your flight.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: N/A – in-flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Post-tour dinner at Da Enzo al 29 (Trastevere) – a beloved Roman trattoria with an upscale casual feel; try cacio e pepe and slow-braised oxtail. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light given afternoon arrival and potential jet lag. Confirm Trastevere tour booking for an evening start time of ~18:30 to align with arrival schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel – Begin with an exclusive early-access skip-the-line guided tour of the Vatican Museums, exploring the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Early morning entry avoids the peak heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross into St. Peter's Basilica for a self-guided exploration of Michelangelo's Pietà and the grand dome. Afterward, stroll along the Tiber River and browse the upscale boutiques near Prati neighborhood. Optional: visit Castel Sant'Angelo for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at Il Sorpasso (Prati) – a stylish bar with an exceptional spread of cicchetti and natural wines. Follow with a premium dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Sciascia Caffè (Prati) – one of Rome's finest historic coffee bars, famous for its thick, velvety espresso and cornetti.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Il Matriciano (Prati) – a classic Roman institution near the Vatican; try rigatoni all'amatriciana and abbacchio al forno.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Convivio Troiani (Centro Storico) – one of Rome's Michelin-starred gems offering creative Roman haute cuisine with an extensive wine cellar. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican early-access tours typically start at 07:30–08:00; book a premium small-group or private guided experience. Dress code enforced at Vatican (covered shoulders and knees). June heat peaks in the afternoon – carry water and wear light, breathable clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour – Enjoy a private or small-group guided tour of the magnificent Villa Borghese Gallery, home to Bernini's breathtaking marble sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks. Entry is strictly timed and limited – a truly intimate world-class experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, take a leisurely walk or electric golf cart ride through the lush Villa Borghese gardens. Descend to the Spanish Steps and explore the luxury shopping street Via Condotti (Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi). Visit the Trevi Fountain in the mid-afternoon when light is golden.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on a rooftop terrace with views over Rome's skyline, followed by dinner in the upscale Parioli or Prati district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Antico Caffè Greco (Via Condotti) – Rome's oldest café (est. 1760), frequented by Keats, Byron, and Goethe; enjoy cappuccino and pastries in gilded surroundings.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nino (Via Borgognona, near Spanish Steps) – a refined Florentine-Roman restaurant beloved by locals and discerning travelers; excellent bistecca and ribollita.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Imàgo at Hotel Hassler – a Michelin-starred rooftop restaurant atop the Spanish Steps offering spectacular panoramic views and refined contemporary Italian cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery requires advance booking (mandatory, max 360 visitors per session). Book tickets 2–4 weeks ahead. Gallery tours last exactly 2 hours. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for the gardens.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Offal Food Tour – Dive deep into Rome's authentic culinary soul at the Mercato Testaccio, the city's finest covered food market. A knowledgeable guide leads you through stalls of seasonal produce, aged cheeses, cured meats, and Rome's famous offal tradition (pajata, trippa, coda alla vaccinara). Sample as you explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Pyramid of Cestius and the Non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) – a hauntingly beautiful and serene garden cemetery where Keats and Shelley are buried. Then explore the Aventine Hill: the Knights of Malta Keyhole (perfect view of St. Peter's dome) and the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) with sweeping river views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Testaccio neighborhood for a vibrant Saturday evening – Rome's most authentic dining district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Roscioli Caffè Pasticceria (Campo de' Fiori area) – Rome's most celebrated artisan bakery-café; outstanding cornetti, pastries, and single-origin espresso.
meals.lunch: Market lunch included in the Testaccio food tour – a generous spread of Roman street food, supplì, porchetta sandwiches, and local wine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) – a legendary Roman restaurant built into the Monte dei Cocci (ancient amphora hill); exceptional cacio e pepe and artichokes alla giudia in a dramatic cave-like setting.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is liveliest on Saturday mornings – arrive by 09:00 with your guide. The food tour lasts approximately 3 hours. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone walking. June temperatures can be warm by midday – the Orange Garden offers welcome shade and breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk – Take a private guided archaeological tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, the birthplace of Rome. Walk where emperors ruled, explore the House of Augustus, the Temple of Vesta, and the Arch of Titus. A private guide brings ancient history vividly to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ascend to the Capitoline Hill and visit the Capitoline Museums – the world's oldest public museums, housing the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and stunning ancient Roman sculpture collections. Enjoy the panoramic terrace view over the Forum.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely evening in the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood – Rome's oldest continuously inhabited community, with beautiful medieval streets, baroque synagogues, and outstanding restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, or at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè (near the Pantheon) – widely regarded as serving Rome's finest espresso, a true Roman institution.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Terrazza Caffarelli (Capitoline Museums rooftop café) – enjoy light Roman fare with one of the most dramatic views in the city overlooking the ancient Forum.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Pagliaccio (Via dei Banchi Vecchi) – Rome's prestigious two-Michelin-starred restaurant offering inventive, ingredient-driven tasting menus that reinterpret Roman and Italian tradition. Reserve months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book combined Forum/Palatine/Colosseum tickets in advance (skip-the-line essential on Sundays). A private guide for 3–4 hours is strongly recommended to fully appreciate the archaeological layers. Capitoline Museums are free on the first Sunday of the month – expect higher visitor numbers.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated art morning: Visit the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj – a magnificent private palazzo still owned by the Doria Pamphilj family, housing an extraordinary private collection including Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and works by Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael. An audio guide narrated by the current prince adds an intimate personal dimension.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pantheon (free entry) – one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world. Then wander through Piazza Navona, admiring Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. Browse the antique map and print dealers along Via della Scrofa. Optional: visit the Museo Nazionale Romano at Palazzo Altemps for more exceptional ancient sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo at a terrace bar overlooking Piazza Navona, followed by a premium cooking class or private chef dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Barnum Café (Campo de' Fiori area) – a charming, design-forward café with excellent specialty coffee and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Rosetta (near the Pantheon) – Rome's most celebrated seafood restaurant, serving pristine Mediterranean fish and shellfish in an elegant setting.
meals.dinner: Private in-home chef dinner experience: book a luxury 'chef at your table' service through a company like Roman Kitchen or Gourmet Experience Rome, where a professional Roman chef prepares a bespoke 5-course seasonal menu with wine pairings in a private historic setting.

day_by_day.notes: Palazzo Doria Pamphilj is closed Thursdays. The Pantheon now charges a small entry fee and requires timed entry booking. June 21st is the summer solstice – the longest day of the year, with sunset around 20:45, perfect for golden-hour photography at Piazza Navona.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure – revisit a favorite neighborhood, do last-minute luxury shopping (Via Condotti, Via del Babuino), or visit the MAXXI (National Museum of 21st Century Arts) for a contrast of contemporary Italian art in Zaha Hadid's stunning architectural landmark in the Flaminio district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout. Depending on departure time, enjoy a final gelato at Giolitti or Fatamorgana (Rome's finest artisan gelato shops). Private luxury transfer to the airport or onward destination.
day_by_day.evening: Departure / travel day

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Caffè della Pace (Piazza della Pace, near Piazza Navona) – one of Rome's most beautiful and atmospheric cafés, draped in ivy with a gorgeous terrace.
meals.lunch: Final lunch at Osteria dell'Enoteca Achilli al Parlamento (near Piazza Colonna) – an outstanding wine bar and restaurant with an encyclopedic cellar and refined Roman cuisine; perfect for a celebratory farewell meal.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and arrange private airport transfer well in advance. MAXXI is closed on Mondays (open Tuesday). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for Rome Fiumicino (FCO) airport, or 1.5 hours for Ciampino (CIA). Consider purchasing a curated selection of Roman artisan products (cured meats, aged cheeses, truffle products, wine) from Roscioli or Volpetti deli as premium take-home gifts.

query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June from Chicago
